questions.stem: Commerce is concerned with
options: the distribution and exchange of goods and services, and the activities that aid them
the extraction of raw materials from the earth and sea only
the manufacture of goods in large factories using machines and skilled labour
the study of how governments make laws
the growing of crops and rearing of animals
questions.explanation: Commerce covers trade and the aids to trade such as banking, transport, insurance, warehousing and communication.

questions.stem: Ada sells handmade beads through her online store and receives payment by bank transfer before delivery by a courier. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Buying and selling goods over the internet with electronic payment is e-commerce.

questions.stem: Banking, insurance, transport, warehousing and communication are grouped together in commerce as
questions.explanation: These services remove hindrances to trade, so they are called aids to trade.

questions.stem: Insurance is regarded as an aid to trade because it removes the hindrance of
questions.explanation: Insurance spreads the risk of loss; warehousing removes time, transport place, banking finance and advertising knowledge hindrances.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of e-commerce to a buyer in Nigeria is that
options: shopping can be done at any time of the day
prices of different sellers can be compared easily
goods cannot be inspected physically before payment
goods are delivered to the buyer's doorstep
the buyer does not need to travel to a market
questions.explanation: The buyer relies on pictures and descriptions and risks fraud or receiving goods that differ from what was advertised.

questions.stem: A major role that commerce plays in an economy is
options: extracting crude oil from wells in the Niger Delta
questions.explanation: Commerce bridges the gap between producers and consumers through trade and its aids.

questions.stem: Before modern commerce developed, the major problem of exchanging goods by barter was the
options: lack of human wants to be satisfied
difficulty of a double coincidence of wants
questions.explanation: Barter needed each trader to want exactly what the other offered.

questions.stem: An occupation may be defined as
options: a place where goods are manufactured
a hobby done only during weekends and public holidays for pleasure
any legal activity a person engages in to earn a living
the training received in a school
any activity that brings no income
questions.explanation: An occupation is the work by which a person earns a living.

questions.stem: Lawyers, teachers and doctors who render personal services directly to people are engaged in
questions.explanation: Direct services are rendered personally to consumers rather than to trade.

questions.stem: A man who builds bridges and houses is engaged in an occupation classified as
questions.explanation: Construction industry builds roads, bridges and houses; it is part of industrial occupation.

questions.stem: Which of the following workers renders an indirect service?
options: A tailor making a dress to order
A gateman employed by a family
questions.explanation: Indirect services are paid for by the state for the community, e.g. police, army and civil service.

questions.stem: The choice of occupation of a young person in Nigeria is least likely to be determined by
options: the colour of his school uniform
the wages and conditions of work offered
his level of education and training
the natural resources in his area
questions.explanation: Education, capital, location, natural resources, family background and expected earnings shape occupational choice.

questions.stem: A woman who buys palm oil from farmers in bulk and resells it to retailers is engaged in a
questions.explanation: Trading activities belong to commercial occupation.

questions.stem: Production in commerce means
options: the consumption of goods by households
the creation of goods and services to satisfy human wants
the storage of goods in warehouses until consumers demand them
the buying of goods for resale only
only the making of goods in factories
questions.explanation: Production includes making goods and providing services until they reach the final consumer.

questions.stem: A sawmill in Sapele that turns logs into planks is engaged in
questions.explanation: Converting raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods is secondary (manufacturing) production.

questions.stem: The production of a whole commodity by one person from start to finish is called
questions.explanation: This is the simplest form, where one craftsman completes the whole article; the opposite is specialisation by process.

questions.stem: An advantage of division of labour to the worker is that
options: his job becomes more interesting and varied
he acquires greater skill through repetition
he can easily change to another job
he controls the whole production process
he works fewer hours for more pay automatically
questions.explanation: Repeating one task develops skill and speed, although it can also cause boredom.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of division of labour is that
options: tools and machines cannot be used efficiently on the factory floor
time is wasted moving from one job to another
the cost of production per unit rises
the worker may become bored and lose craftsmanship
questions.explanation: Monotony, loss of craftsmanship and interdependence are drawbacks of specialisation.

questions.stem: Production and exchange are interrelated because
options: production stops whenever goods are exchanged
exchange is carried out only by government
specialised producers exchange surpluses for what they lack
exchange happens only when there is no production
producers consume everything they make and so need not exchange
questions.explanation: Specialisation creates surpluses that must be traded, and exchange allows producers to specialise.

questions.stem: Land, labour, capital and entrepreneur are together called
questions.explanation: These are the resources combined to produce goods and services.

questions.stem: The legal document that regulates the internal affairs of a limited company, such as the rights of members and the conduct of meetings, is the
questions.explanation: The articles govern internal management; the memorandum defines the company's relationship with outsiders.

questions.stem: Under the Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, a private company in Nigeria
options: can invite the public to buy its shares
must list its shares on the stock exchange
may be formed by a single person
has unlimited liability in all cases
must have at least seven members
questions.explanation: CAMA 2020 allows a private company to be incorporated by one person.

questions.stem: A partner who contributes capital but takes no part in managing the business and whose liability is limited is a
questions.explanation: A limited partner's liability is limited to the capital contributed, and he may not take part in management.

questions.stem: Which document must a public company in Nigeria issue when inviting the public to subscribe for its shares?
questions.explanation: The prospectus gives information to the public about the company and the shares on offer.

questions.stem: The section of the memorandum of association which states the activities a company is formed to carry out is the
questions.explanation: The objects clause sets out the business the company may undertake.

questions.stem: A co-operative society in which farmers jointly market their cocoa to obtain better prices is a
questions.explanation: Producers' co-operatives help members process and market their output collectively.

questions.stem: The combination of two companies in the same line of business to form a completely new company is
questions.explanation: In amalgamation both companies lose their identities and form a new one.

questions.stem: A company that owns enough shares in other companies to control them is a
questions.explanation: The holding company controls its subsidiaries through majority shareholding.

questions.stem: A group of independent firms that agree to fix prices or share markets while remaining separate businesses is a
questions.explanation: A cartel restricts competition by agreements on price or output among independent firms.

questions.stem: The main source of capital for a sole trader is
options: floating bonds on the stock exchange
sale of shares to the public
questions.explanation: Sole traders rely mainly on their own savings, plus loans from friends, relatives and banks.

questions.stem: The winding up of a company ordered by a court, for example on a creditor's petition, is called
questions.explanation: Compulsory (court-ordered) winding up often follows inability to pay debts.

questions.stem: An association formed by businesses in the same trade to protect and promote their common interests is a
questions.explanation: Trade associations represent firms in the same trade, unlike trade unions which represent workers.

questions.stem: The Manufacturers Association of Nigeria (MAN) is an example of
options: a trade union of factory workers
a trade association of manufacturing firms
a consumer protection association of buyers
a chamber of commerce for importers
questions.explanation: MAN represents manufacturers' interests in dealings with government and others.

questions.stem: A function of a chamber of commerce such as the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry is to
options: organise trade fairs and provide business information to members
fix the minimum wage for workers
questions.explanation: Chambers of commerce promote trade through fairs, information, advocacy and certification.

questions.stem: The Nigeria Employers' Consultative Association (NECA) mainly
options: insures the deposits of bank customers
regulates the activities of the stock exchange
represents factory workers in wage negotiations with employers and with government
represents employers in negotiations with labour unions and government
questions.explanation: NECA is the umbrella body of employers on labour and social matters.

questions.stem: When consumers in a town organise themselves to demand safe products, fair prices and honest advertising, they are practising
questions.explanation: Consumerism seeks fair prices, safe goods, honest information and redress for consumers.

questions.stem: One aim of a consumer association is to
options: educate consumers about their rights and fight exploitation
fix prices of goods above market levels
sell goods to members at a profit
questions.explanation: Consumer associations inform consumers and press for protection against unfair practices.

questions.stem: The ceiling on the share capital a company may issue, traditionally stated in its memorandum, is its
questions.explanation: Authorised (registered or nominal) capital is the ceiling of share capital in the memorandum; CAMA 2020 now speaks of minimum issued share capital.

questions.stem: A trader has current assets of ₦850,000 and current liabilities of ₦320,000. Her working capital is
questions.explanation: Working capital = current assets − current liabilities = 850,000 − 320,000 = ₦530,000.

questions.stem: A company has issued 2,000,000 shares of ₦1 each and has asked shareholders to pay 75 kobo per share so far, all of which has been paid. Its called-up capital is
The capital that is constantly changing form in the course of trading, such as stock, debtors and cash, is called
questions.explanation: Circulating (liquid) capital flows through the trading cycle from cash to stock to debtors and back.

questions.stem: Goods costing ₦400,000 were sold for ₦520,000, and expenses of ₦45,000 were paid. The net profit is
A trader's opening stock was ₦60,000 and closing stock was ₦40,000. If her cost of goods sold was ₦300,000, her rate of turnover is
questions.explanation: Average stock = (60,000 + 40,000)/2 = 50,000; rate of turnover = 300,000/50,000 = 6 times.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper buys an item for ₦8,000 and sells it for ₦10,000. Her gross profit as a percentage of the selling price (margin) is
questions.explanation: Margin = 2,000/10,000 × 100 = 20%; mark-up on cost would be 25%.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a credit instrument?
options: A delivery note signed by the buyer
questions.explanation: A promissory note is a written promise to pay a sum at a future date, used to grant credit.

questions.stem: The rate of turnover of a business is likely to increase if
options: the goods sold are expensive durables bought only once in years
the business keeps very high stock levels
the business reduces its prices and advertises more
questions.explanation: Lower prices and effective advertising speed up sales, increasing turnover.

questions.stem: Credit in commerce means
options: obtaining goods or money now and paying later
paying cash for goods at once
questions.explanation: Credit is a facility allowing a buyer or borrower to pay at a future date.

questions.stem: A retailer is the last link in the chain of distribution because he
options: sells goods directly to the final consumer
questions.explanation: Retailers sell to consumers, completing the chain from producer to consumer.

questions.stem: A large shop divided into sections, each selling different kinds of goods under one roof and one management, is a
questions.explanation: A department store is like many shops in one building under one management.

questions.stem: A retail business with branches in many towns, all selling similar goods, looking alike and controlled from one head office, is
questions.explanation: Multiples have branches in many towns with central buying and uniform appearance.

questions.stem: A form of retailing in which customers pick goods themselves from open shelves and pay at a checkout is
questions.explanation: Self-service is common in supermarkets and reduces staff costs.

questions.stem: Which factor favours the survival of the wholesaler in Nigeria despite moves to eliminate middlemen?
options: Manufacturers prefer to keep large stocks themselves
Retailers have large capital to buy directly from producers
Many small retailers need to buy in small quantities on credit
questions.explanation: Small retailers cannot buy in bulk from manufacturers, so wholesalers break bulk and give credit.

questions.stem: A function of the wholesaler to the manufacturer is
options: selling goods to final consumers in small units
buying in bulk and relieving him of storage problems
producing raw materials for the factory
questions.explanation: By buying in bulk, the wholesaler finances production and stores goods.

questions.stem: A merchant wholesaler differs from an agent wholesaler in that the merchant wholesaler
options: sells on commission without owning the goods
takes ownership of the goods he sells
questions.explanation: Merchant wholesalers buy and own goods; agent wholesalers sell for principals on commission.

questions.stem: A trader who carries goods on her head from street to street selling to passers-by is a
questions.explanation: Hawkers move about with their goods instead of operating from a fixed shop.

questions.stem: The route by which goods move from the producer to the consumer is called
questions.explanation: Channels of distribution may include wholesalers, retailers and agents, or go direct.

questions.stem: A manufacturer of cement is likely to sell directly to building contractors rather than through retailers because
options: consumers buy cement in very small quantities
the product is bulky and bought in large quantities by few buyers
questions.explanation: Large orders from a few industrial buyers favour a direct channel.

questions.stem: A modern trend in retailing in which goods are sold by machines that accept coins, notes or cards is
questions.explanation: Vending machines are automatic retail outlets.

questions.stem: When a Lagos trader buys shea butter from a supplier in Tamale, Ghana, the transaction is
questions.explanation: Trade across national borders is foreign (international) trade.

questions.stem: Goods imported into a country, stored or repacked there and then sent on to other countries without being consumed locally, are part of
questions.explanation: Entrepot trade involves importing goods, sometimes repacking them, and re-exporting them.

questions.stem: If a country's visible exports are worth ₦12 billion and its visible imports ₦15 billion, it has
options: a favourable balance of trade of ₦3 billion
a balance of payments surplus of ₦27 billion
an unfavourable balance of trade of ₦3 billion
a favourable balance of payments of ₦3 billion
questions.explanation: Balance of trade = 12 − 15 = −₦3 billion, an unfavourable balance.

questions.stem: Freight charges earned by a Nigerian shipping line from carrying goods for foreigners are
questions.explanation: Services sold to foreigners are invisible exports.

questions.stem: An agreement between two countries to exchange goods directly without using money is
questions.explanation: Counter trade, such as oil-for-goods deals, exchanges goods without currency.

questions.stem: The selling of goods abroad at prices lower than those charged in the home market, sometimes below cost, is called
questions.explanation: Dumping can harm local industries in the importing country.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for collecting import and excise duties at Nigerian borders and ports is the
questions.explanation: The Nigeria Customs Service collects duties and controls goods entering and leaving the country.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC) helps exporters mainly by
options: providing information on export markets and incentives
collecting import duties at the ports
questions.explanation: NEPC promotes non-oil exports through market information, training and incentives.

questions.stem: An agent who handles the documentation and customs procedures needed to get imported goods out of the port is a
questions.explanation: Clearing and forwarding agents clear goods through customs and arrange onward transport.

questions.stem: When the Nigeria Customs Service charges a percentage of the value of a consignment of imported generators, the charge is
questions.explanation: Import duties are taxes on goods entering a country.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: Mrs Bello, a retailer in Ilorin, writes to a wholesaler asking him to supply 50 cartons of noodles at the quoted price. The document she sends is
questions.explanation: The order states the goods wanted, quantity, price and delivery terms.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: Mr Okafor received too many crates of soft drinks and returned the excess to the supplier. The supplier will send him
options: an advice note sent before dispatch
a consular invoice certified by an embassy
questions.explanation: A credit note reduces the amount the buyer owes, for returns or overcharges.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: An invoice sent to a buyer before goods are dispatched, often so that the buyer can pay in advance or obtain an import licence, is
questions.explanation: A pro forma invoice is a preliminary invoice showing what the full invoice would contain.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: Goods with a catalogue price of ₦50,000 are sold to a retailer at 20% trade discount and 5% cash discount for prompt payment. If the retailer pays promptly, the amount paid is
questions.explanation: Trade discount: 50,000 − 10,000 = 40,000; cash discount 5% of 40,000 = 2,000; amount paid = ₦38,000.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A price quotation "C.I.F. Lagos" means the price includes
options: cost of the goods, insurance and freight to Lagos
cost of the goods only at the seller's factory
cost of goods delivered alongside the ship at the port of loading
carriage paid by the buyer from the factory
the commission of the clearing agent in Lagos
questions.explanation: C.I.F. covers cost, insurance and freight to the named port of destination.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: Under an "ex-works" quotation, the buyer bears
options: only costs after the goods arrive at the port of destination
all costs from the seller's premises onwards
questions.explanation: Ex-works (loco) prices cover only the goods at the factory; the buyer pays all carriage.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: The abbreviation E. & O.E. printed on an invoice means
questions.explanation: It allows the seller to correct mistakes later.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A document, signed by the consul of the importing country, which confirms the value and origin of goods for customs purposes, is
questions.explanation: Consular invoices help the importing country's customs to assess duty and prevent under-invoicing.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A written, unconditional order by one person to another to pay a stated sum on demand or at a fixed future date is
options: a promissory note signed by the debtor
questions.explanation: The drawer orders the drawee to pay; a promissory note is instead a promise to pay.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: A customer instructs her bank to pay her monthly rent of ₦150,000 to her landlord on the 1st of every month. This is
questions.explanation: A standing order is a regular payment made by the bank on the customer's instruction.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem: An order placed by an importer with an agent abroad to buy goods on his behalf is called
questions.explanation: An indent is an order sent to a foreign commission agent.

questions.stem: For an item to serve well as money in a modern economy, it should possess
questions.explanation: Good money should be portable, durable, divisible, homogeneous, acceptable and difficult to forge.

questions.stem: When a trader saves ₦200,000 to buy goods next year, money is serving as
questions.explanation: Money can be kept and used later; that is its store-of-value function.

questions.stem: Cowries and manillas were used in parts of West Africa as
questions.explanation: Objects with intrinsic value used as money are commodity money.

questions.stem: Legal tender in Nigeria refers to
options: bills of exchange accepted by banks
naira notes and coins that must be accepted in payment of debts
cheques issued by deposit money banks and accepted by traders in every market
any foreign currency held in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Legal tender is money that the law requires creditors to accept, issued by the CBN.

questions.stem: The currency of Nigeria, the naira, was introduced on 1 January 1973 to replace the
questions.explanation: The naira and kobo replaced the Nigerian pound in January 1973.

questions.stem: The type of bank account on which cheques are drawn is
questions.explanation: Current account holders receive cheque books and may draw cheques.

questions.stem: A customer who will not need ₦2 million for one year and wants the highest interest from a bank should open
options: an ordinary savings account with a passbook
questions.explanation: Fixed deposits pay higher interest because funds are locked for an agreed period.

questions.stem: Microfinance banks in Nigeria mainly
options: provide small loans and savings services to low-income people and small businesses
supervise and regulate all the other banks in the country
questions.explanation: Microfinance banks serve small enterprises and low-income earners neglected by bigger banks.

questions.stem: A bureau de change mainly
options: sells shares on the stock exchange
issues cheque books to all customers who maintain current accounts
buys and sells foreign currencies to the public
questions.explanation: BDCs deal in retail foreign exchange.

questions.stem: Emeka sends ₦25,000 from his bank account to his sister's account in another bank using his phone. This is an example of
questions.explanation: Mobile and internet transfers are forms of electronic banking.

questions.stem: A mortgage bank differs from a commercial bank because it
options: deals only in foreign exchange for travellers and importers
accepts deposits only from the government
grants long-term loans mainly for building or buying houses
questions.explanation: Mortgage institutions specialise in long-term housing finance secured on property.

questions.stem: A cheque crossed "Account Payee only" must be
options: cashed over the counter by anyone who presents it at the bank
paid into the account of the named payee
questions.explanation: This crossing restricts payment to the payee's bank account.

questions.stem: An Automated Teller Machine (ATM) enables bank customers to
options: withdraw cash at any time without entering the banking hall
print new cheque books for themselves and their family members
borrow money from the Central Bank
questions.explanation: ATMs provide cash withdrawals and other services round the clock.

questions.stem: The amount paid periodically by the insured to the insurer for cover is the
questions.explanation: The premium is the price of insurance cover.

questions.stem: The principle of insurance which requires the insured to disclose all material facts when applying for a policy is
options: proximate cause of the loss suffered
questions.explanation: Both parties must reveal all relevant facts; non-disclosure can void the policy.

questions.stem: A person can insure only property in whose loss he would suffer financially. This is the principle of
questions.explanation: Insurable interest requires a financial stake in the subject matter.

questions.stem: After paying a claim for a stolen car, an insurance company takes over the owner's rights against the thief and to any recovered car. This is the principle of
questions.explanation: Subrogation passes the insured's rights to the insurer after the claim is settled.

questions.stem: A building is insured with Company X for ₦3 million and with Company Y for ₦2 million. A fire causes damage worth ₦1 million. Under the principle of contribution, Company X will pay
A shop worth ₦10 million is insured for ₦6 million under a policy with an average clause. A fire causes loss of ₦2 million. The insurer will pay
questions.explanation: Payment = loss × sum insured/value = 2,000,000 × 6/10 = ₦1,200,000.

questions.stem: Mr Danjuma takes out a 15-year life policy that will pay him a lump sum when it matures, or pay his family if he dies before then. This is
questions.explanation: Endowment policies combine saving with protection for a fixed term.

questions.stem: A boutique owner in Abuja seeks insurance cover. The risk for which no insurer will give cover is
options: Damage to a car in an accident
loss of sales when fashions change
Loss from burglary of a shop
questions.explanation: Speculative trading losses cannot be calculated statistically and are uninsurable.

questions.stem: An insurer who has accepted a very large risk passes part of it to another insurer. This is called
questions.explanation: Re-insurance spreads large risks among insurers.

questions.stem: An insurance policy that protects an employer against loss from dishonesty of his employees is
questions.explanation: Fidelity guarantee covers losses from fraud or theft by employees.

questions.stem: A manufacturer needing finance for a new factory to be repaid over fifteen years would approach the capital market because it deals in
options: short-term funds repayable within a few months only
questions.explanation: The capital market raises long-term finance through shares, bonds and similar securities.

questions.stem: A company that offers new shares to its existing shareholders in proportion to their holdings is making
questions.explanation: A rights issue gives current shareholders the right to buy new shares, usually at a discount.

questions.stem: A company makes a rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 held. A shareholder who owns 2,000 shares is entitled to
When a company sells its new shares to a few selected institutional investors instead of the general public, it is using
questions.explanation: Private placement sells securities directly to chosen investors.

questions.stem: In an offer for sale, the company's new shares are
options: sold by auction to the highest bidders only
sold directly by the company to members of the public by means of a prospectus
first sold to an issuing house which then resells them to the public
questions.explanation: The issuing house buys the whole issue and resells it, bearing the risk.

questions.stem: The government agency that regulates the Nigerian capital market is the
questions.explanation: The SEC registers and supervises securities, exchanges and market operators.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) is a market where
options: existing securities such as shares and bonds are bought and sold
goods such as yams and rice are auctioned
foreign currencies are exchanged by tourists arriving at the airports
questions.explanation: A stock exchange is a secondary market for listed securities.

questions.stem: A speculator on the stock exchange who buys shares expecting their prices to rise so as to sell at a profit is a
questions.explanation: Bulls buy in expectation of a price rise; bears sell expecting a fall.

questions.stem: A speculator who applies for new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a premium once trading begins is a
questions.explanation: Stags subscribe to new issues for a quick profit.

questions.stem: An investor holds 20,000 ordinary shares in a company that declares a dividend of 50 kobo per share. The investor receives
Holders of debentures differ from shareholders because debenture holders
options: receive dividends only when profits are made and declared by the directors
have voting rights at annual general meetings
are creditors who receive fixed interest whether or not there is profit
bear the greatest risk of loss
questions.explanation: Debentures are loans to the company and attract fixed interest.

questions.stem: Federal Government of Nigeria bonds are described as gilt-edged securities because
options: they are sold only to foreigners
the risk of default on them is very low
they are shares in government companies
they pay the highest returns in the market
questions.explanation: Government securities are regarded as very safe investments.

questions.stem: The type of share whose holders receive a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid is
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders have priority for a fixed dividend.

questions.stem: A maize farmer in Kaduna who deposits graded maize in a certified warehouse and sells it through a commodity exchange is using a market where
options: foreign currencies are traded by banks
standardised farm and mineral products are traded
questions.explanation: Commodity exchanges trade graded commodities such as grains, cocoa and metals, often through contracts.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a commodity exchange operating in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: NCX, based in Abuja, provides a platform for trading commodities; NGX is a securities exchange.

questions.stem: Before a commodity can be traded on a commodity exchange it must be
questions.explanation: Grading ensures that buyers know the quality without inspecting each lot.

questions.stem: A method of trading on a commodity exchange in which traders shout and use hand signals on the trading floor is
questions.explanation: Open outcry is the traditional floor-trading method; most exchanges now trade electronically.

questions.stem: Cocoa and sesame farmers who sell through an organised commodity exchange benefit because it
options: gives a transparent market and fairer prices
fixes the prices of all crops by law for every season
buys all crops whether graded or not
questions.explanation: Organised markets improve price discovery and reduce exploitation by middlemen.

questions.stem: Transport aids trade mainly by removing the hindrance of
questions.explanation: Transport moves goods from where they are produced to where they are needed.

questions.stem: The most suitable means of transporting crude oil from the Niger Delta to a refinery inland is
questions.explanation: Pipelines carry liquids and gases cheaply and continuously over long distances.

questions.stem: A document listing all the cargo carried on a ship or aircraft is the
questions.explanation: The manifest is the list of all cargo on board, used by customs and port officials.

questions.stem: A major advantage of air transport over sea transport is
options: independence from weather conditions at all times
lower freight charges for bulky goods
ability to carry very heavy cargo cheaply
speed of delivery for urgent and perishable goods
questions.explanation: Air transport is fastest, though expensive and limited in bulk.

questions.stem: A trader in Kano sending a consignment of goods by rail to Lagos will receive from the railway a document called
questions.explanation: A consignment note accompanies goods sent by rail or road; a bill of lading is for sea.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of road transport in Nigeria is
options: the poor condition of many roads and high accident rates
its rigidity of fixed routes and timetables compared with rail
that it is slower than walking
its inability to provide door-to-door service
questions.explanation: Bad roads, congestion, accidents and insecurity limit road transport.

questions.stem: The choice of transport for a particular consignment is least likely to be affected by
questions.explanation: Cost, speed, safety, nature of goods and distance determine the choice.

questions.stem: A family from Lagos that spends its holiday at Obudu Mountain Resort in Cross River State is engaged in
questions.explanation: Travel within one's own country for leisure is domestic tourism.

questions.stem: An economic advantage of tourism to a country such as Nigeria is that it
options: always protects local culture from change
earns foreign exchange and creates jobs
questions.explanation: Tourism brings foreign exchange, employment and demand for local goods and services.

questions.stem: Residents near the Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove complain that the crowds of visitors are changing local customs and littering the grove. This shows that tourism can
options: bring foreign exchange into the economy
erode local culture and damage the environment
promote the sale of local crafts to visitors from abroad
questions.explanation: Large numbers of visitors can damage sites and change local customs.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Postal Service (NIPOST) provides
options: loans to small businesses and farmers in rural areas
delivery of letters and parcels and other postal services
questions.explanation: NIPOST offers mail, parcel, courier and related services.

questions.stem: The agency that regulates telecommunications services, including mobile networks, in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The NCC licenses and regulates telecommunications operators.

questions.stem: A form of communication in which a manager speaks face to face with her staff at a meeting is
questions.explanation: Spoken communication, face to face or by phone, is oral communication.

questions.stem: A courier service is preferred to ordinary post for sending important business documents mainly because it
options: is faster and offers tracking and door-to-door delivery
carries only heavy machinery and building materials between states
questions.explanation: Courier firms deliver quickly, securely and can trace items.

questions.stem: In computer appreciation, the part of a computer that processes data and controls other parts is the
questions.explanation: The CPU performs processing and control; the others are input or output devices.

questions.stem: Sending a message electronically from one computer to another over the internet is
questions.explanation: E-mail is the electronic transmission of messages over computer networks.

questions.stem: Warehousing aids trade by removing the hindrance of
questions.explanation: Storing goods until they are needed bridges the gap between production and consumption.

questions.stem: An importer of wines at Apapa who cannot yet pay the duty may leave the goods under customs control in
options: a cold room in a supermarket
questions.explanation: Bonded warehouses hold dutiable goods under customs control.

questions.stem: An advantage of the bonded warehouse to an importer is that
options: goods can be sold without customs documents
duty can be paid in instalments as goods are withdrawn
the warehouse owner pays the duty on behalf of the importer
goods are stored free of charge for ever
no duty is ever paid on the goods
questions.explanation: The importer pays duty only on goods taken out, easing cash flow.

questions.stem: Warehouses owned by the government or by companies that rent storage space to anyone are
questions.explanation: Public warehouses offer storage to all traders for a fee.

questions.stem: Warehousing helps to stabilise prices of seasonal goods because
options: it destroys excess goods during harvest
it prevents goods from being sold
prices are fixed by warehouse owners
goods stored at harvest can be released during scarcity
it increases production costs and so raises the prices of seasonal goods
questions.explanation: Storage evens out supply over the year, reducing price fluctuations.

questions.stem: Advertising which aims mainly to tell the public about the existence and features of a new product is
questions.explanation: Informative advertising provides facts about products and services.

questions.stem: Advertising designed to win customers from rival brands by claiming one's product is better is
questions.explanation: Competitive advertising compares a product favourably with rivals.

questions.stem: The body that regulates the practice of advertising in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: ARCON, formerly APCON, regulates advertising practice and content in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Critics of the many billboards along the Lagos–Ibadan Expressway argue that advertising can
options: persuade people to buy things they do not need
inform consumers about new products and their uses
questions.explanation: Persuasive advertising can create artificial wants and raise costs.

questions.stem: A manufacturer wishing to reach a large, mostly illiterate audience in rural areas cheaply would most likely use
options: an internet banner on a financial website
advertisements in a national business newspaper
questions.explanation: Radio in local languages reaches many rural listeners regardless of literacy.

questions.stem: Advertising through samples, window displays and trade exhibitions is described as
questions.explanation: These methods promote goods without using mass media.

questions.stem: A medium of advertising that combines sound and moving pictures is
questions.explanation: Television combines sound and vision.

questions.stem: Marketing involves
options: only selling goods at the market
manufacturing goods in factories and storing them in warehouses
identifying customers' needs and satisfying them profitably
questions.explanation: Marketing covers research, product design, pricing, distribution and promotion.

questions.stem: A soap maker that studies only the size and buying habits of the Onitsha market is doing market research rather than marketing research, because market research
options: studies a particular market and its customers only
covers all aspects of marketing including pricing and promotion
questions.explanation: Market research focuses on the market; marketing research is wider, covering all marketing activities.

questions.stem: A firm surveys 500 households in Enugu to find out whether they would buy a new brand of noodles. This activity is
questions.explanation: Collecting information about potential customers and demand is market research.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: The marketing mix consists of
questions.explanation: The 4Ps are product, price, place and promotion.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: When a beverage company decides whether to sell its drinks through supermarkets, kiosks or online platforms, it is deciding on which element of the marketing mix?
questions.explanation: Place covers channels of distribution and where customers can obtain the product.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: The marketing concept holds that a business should
options: sell goods at the highest possible price regardless of customers' wishes
produce what it can and then persuade people to buy
find out what customers want and produce to satisfy them
questions.explanation: The marketing concept puts customer needs at the centre of business decisions.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem: A firm introduces a new smartphone at a low price to win a large share of the market quickly. This pricing strategy is
questions.explanation: Penetration pricing uses low initial prices to gain market share.

questions.stem: Services provided to a customer after the purchase of a refrigerator, such as installation and repairs under warranty, are
questions.explanation: After-sales services support the customer after purchase.

questions.stem: Demonstrating how a generator works to a prospective buyer before he decides to buy it is an example of
questions.explanation: Pre-sales services help customers choose before buying.

questions.stem: Good customer service is important to a business mainly because it
options: builds customer loyalty and repeat purchases
eliminates competition from rival firms by law
questions.explanation: Satisfied customers return and recommend the business.

questions.stem: Giving free gifts, coupons and discounts to increase sales over a short period is known as
questions.explanation: Sales promotion uses short-term incentives to boost sales.

questions.stem: Exhibitions where many firms display their goods and services to the public and other businesses, such as the Lagos International Trade Fair, are
questions.explanation: Trade fairs bring producers and buyers together to display and sell goods.

questions.stem: Personal selling is particularly useful for
options: technical or costly products that need explanation
goods sold only by mail order
questions.explanation: Sales representatives can explain, demonstrate and answer questions.

questions.stem: A legally binding agreement between two or more parties is
questions.explanation: A contract is an agreement enforceable by law.

questions.stem: The display of goods with price tags in a shop window is regarded in law as
questions.explanation: Displays invite customers to make offers; they are not offers themselves.

questions.stem: Something of value given by each party to a contract, such as money for goods, is called
questions.explanation: Consideration is the price paid for the other party's promise.

questions.stem: A contract may be discharged by frustration when
options: the parties agree to cancel it
the price is paid in advance
an unforeseen event makes performance impossible
questions.explanation: Frustration occurs when events beyond the parties' control make performance impossible.

questions.stem: A contract to supply stolen goods is not valid because it lacks
questions.explanation: Contracts for illegal purposes are void.

questions.stem: A person authorised to act on behalf of another in dealings with third parties is
questions.explanation: The agent acts for the principal.

questions.stem: An agent who, for an extra commission, guarantees that the buyers he finds will pay is
questions.explanation: Del credere agents bear the risk of bad debts in return for extra commission.

questions.stem: When a principal approves a contract made by an agent who acted without authority, agency is created by
questions.explanation: Ratification is later approval, which makes the contract binding.

questions.stem: A duty of an agent to his principal is to
options: obey lawful instructions and render accounts
delegate all his work to others
act for rival principals without consent
questions.explanation: Agents must obey instructions, use skill, act in good faith and account for money.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: Under the Sale of Goods Act, a condition implied in a sale by sample is that
options: the goods need not be fit for use
the seller need not have title
the seller may deliver any quality
the buyer must pay before inspection
the bulk will correspond with the sample
questions.explanation: Goods sold by sample must match the sample in quality.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: Kemi buys a television on hire purchase, paying ₦30,000 monthly for ten months. She becomes the legal owner of the television
options: never, as it remains the seller's property
when the last instalment is paid
when the television is delivered to her
when the first instalment is paid
questions.explanation: The owner retains title until all instalments are paid.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: A major difference between hire purchase and credit sale is that under credit sale
options: ownership passes to the buyer immediately
the seller can repossess goods at any time
the buyer never owns the goods
payment must be made in cash at once
questions.explanation: In credit sale title passes at once and the seller can only sue for the debt.

questions.topic: Sale of Goods Act, Hire Purchase Act and Employment Rights
questions.stem: A right of an employee under employment laws in Nigeria is
options: to receive wages as agreed in the contract of employment
to take the employer's property home
questions.explanation: Employees are entitled to agreed wages, safe working conditions and proper notice.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: In Nigeria, companies and business names are registered by the
questions.explanation: The CAC registers companies, business names and incorporated trustees under CAMA 2020.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: An engineer in Nnewi designs a new motorcycle part and wants to stop others from copying and selling it for a number of years. She should obtain
options: a franchise agreement with a dealer
questions.explanation: A patent protects inventions.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: A musician's exclusive right to reproduce and sell her songs is protected by
questions.explanation: Copyright protects original literary, musical and artistic works.

questions.topic: Government Regulation and Registration of Business
questions.stem: A distinctive symbol or name used by a firm to distinguish its goods from those of others is protected as
questions.explanation: Registered trade marks protect brand identity.

questions.stem: A bakery in Asaba wants to sell packaged bread in supermarkets. The product must first be registered with the agency that regulates processed food, which is
questions.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control regulates these products.

questions.stem: The federal body that enforces consumer protection and competition law in Nigeria is the
options: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission
questions.explanation: FCCPC was established under the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018.

questions.stem: Fake drugs, adulterated palm oil and short-measured fuel at some filling stations illustrate why
options: producers need tariff protection from imports
questions.explanation: Exploitation through adulteration, false weights and misleading claims makes protection necessary.

questions.stem: The Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) protects consumers mainly by
options: setting and enforcing quality standards for products
questions.explanation: SON sets product standards and checks compliance.

questions.stem: The sale of government-owned enterprises or shares in them to private investors is
questions.explanation: Privatisation transfers ownership to the private sector.

questions.stem: The removal of government controls on prices and entry into an industry, such as the downstream petroleum sector, is called
questions.explanation: Deregulation removes restrictions so market forces operate.

questions.stem: Under commercialisation, a public enterprise
options: is sold completely to private investors through core investors and the stock exchange
remains government-owned but is run to cover its costs and make profit
questions.explanation: Commercialisation keeps state ownership but requires commercial operation.

questions.stem: The agency that implements the Federal Government's privatisation programme in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The BPE is the secretariat of the National Council on Privatisation.

questions.stem: A disadvantage of deregulation of the downstream petroleum sector to consumers is that
questions.explanation: Removing price controls and subsidy exposes consumers to market prices.

questions.stem: The management function of setting objectives and deciding in advance how to achieve them is
questions.explanation: Planning sets goals and the means of reaching them.

questions.stem: The number of subordinates a manager directly supervises is called
questions.explanation: Span of control measures how many people report to one superior.

options: the manager doing all the work personally without any help from staff
giving a subordinate authority while the manager stays accountable
questions.explanation: Delegation passes authority but not ultimate responsibility.

questions.stem: Money, materials, machines, manpower and goodwill are together called
questions.explanation: These are the resources a business manages to achieve its goals.

questions.stem: A cement company that builds a health centre and repairs roads in its host community is fulfilling its
questions.explanation: Social responsibility is the duty of business to contribute to the welfare of society.

questions.stem: A diagram showing the departments of a firm and the lines of authority and responsibility among them is
questions.explanation: The organisational chart shows structure and reporting lines.

questions.stem: The headquarters of the Economic Community of West African States is in
questions.explanation: The ECOWAS Commission is in Abuja.

questions.stem: The Mano River Union was formed in 1973 by
questions.explanation: Guinea joined in 1980 and Côte d'Ivoire in 2008.

questions.stem: The Lake Chad Basin Commission was established in 1964 mainly to
options: promote a single currency for all the countries of West Africa
manage the stock exchanges of member states
manage the use of the lake's waters and resources
questions.explanation: LCBC co-ordinates the use of the lake's water and resources among member states.

questions.stem: In the 1970s West African central banks created an arrangement that allowed member countries to settle trade payments with one another in their own currencies. This was the
options: ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development

excess good roads and railways linking all member states
