options: Niger Basin Authority (formerly Niger River Commission)
questions.explanation: The Niger Basin Authority, with headquarters in Niamey, succeeded the Niger River Commission.

questions.stem:
(a) Define e-commerce. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of commerce. [8 marks]
(c) State five ways in which e-commerce has changed the way Nigerian businesses buy and sell. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The buying and selling of goods and services, and transfer of payment, over electronic networks, mainly the internet and mobile phones (2)
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: links producers and consumers; facilitates exchange of goods and services; removes hindrances to trade through aids to trade; creates employment; raises living standards by making varied goods available; promotes international relations through foreign trade
10 marks: (c) Any five, 2 marks each: online stores and marketplaces; payment by transfer, cards and USSD; social media advertising and selling; online ordering and doorstep delivery; 24-hour trading; wider (national/international) market reach; lower cost of shop premises; electronic invoices and receipts; easier price comparison by buyers
questions.explanation: (a) E-commerce is trade carried out through electronic means such as websites, apps and mobile platforms, with electronic payment. (b) Commerce links producers with consumers, enables exchange, removes hindrances of place, time, risk, finance and knowledge through transport, warehousing, insurance, banking and advertising, creates jobs and raises living standards. (c) Nigerian firms now sell through online marketplaces and social media, receive payment by transfer, cards and USSD, deliver to customers' doors, trade round the clock, reach buyers far beyond their towns, cut the cost of shop premises and allow buyers to compare prices easily.

questions.stem:
(a) What is an occupation? [2 marks]
(b) Explain with an example each: (i) industrial occupation; (ii) commercial occupation; (iii) direct services; (iv) indirect services. [12 marks]
(c) State three factors that influence a person's choice of occupation. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) Any legal activity in which a person engages to earn a living (2)
3 marks: (b)(i) Industrial: extraction, manufacturing and construction, e.g. mining, tailoring, building (2 for explanation, 1 for example)
3 marks: (b)(ii) Commercial: trade and aids to trade, e.g. retailing, banking, transport (2 + 1)
3 marks: (b)(iii) Direct services: personal services rendered directly to individuals who pay for them, e.g. doctors, lawyers, barbers (2 + 1)
3 marks: (b)(iv) Indirect services: services to the community paid by government, e.g. police, soldiers, civil servants (2 + 1)
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: education and training; capital available; natural resources of the area; family background; personal interest/aptitude; remuneration and conditions of service; government policy; level of technology
questions.explanation: (a) An occupation is any lawful work a person does to earn a living. (b) Industrial occupations produce goods through extraction (fishing, mining), manufacturing (bakery) or construction (building). Commercial occupations involve trade (retailing) and aids to trade (banking, transport, insurance). Direct services are rendered personally to people who pay directly, such as doctors and hairdressers. Indirect services benefit the community and are paid for by government, such as the police and civil servants. (c) Choice of occupation depends on education and training, available capital, local resources, family background, interest, pay and conditions, and government policy.

questions.stem:
(a) Define division of labour. [2 marks]
(b) Explain four advantages of division of labour. [8 marks]
(c) Explain three disadvantages of division of labour. [6 marks]
(d) State two factors that limit division of labour. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The breaking down of the production of a commodity into separate processes or tasks, each performed by a different worker or group (2)
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: increased output; greater skill through repetition; saving of time; use of machines encouraged; workers do what they are best suited for; lower cost per unit; better quality goods; encourages inventions
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: boredom/monotony; loss of craftsmanship; interdependence so a breakdown stops production; unemployment from mechanisation; limited job mobility; loss of responsibility/pride
4 marks: (d) Any two, 2 marks each: size of the market; nature of the product; availability of capital; level of technology; availability of skilled labour
questions.explanation: (a) Division of labour splits the production of a commodity into processes, each handled by different workers. (b) It raises output, develops skill through repetition, saves time lost in moving between tasks, encourages the use of machines, lets each worker do what he does best and lowers unit costs. (c) It causes monotony, loss of craftsmanship, dangerous interdependence where one section's stoppage halts the whole line, and possible unemployment. (d) It is limited by the size of the market, the nature of the product, available capital and technology.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five differences between a partnership and a public limited company. [10 marks]
(b) State three sources of capital available to a public limited company. [6 marks]
(c) Explain two ways in which a partnership may be dissolved. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) Any five, 2 marks each: formation (partnership deed vs registration with CAC under CAMA with memorandum and articles); liability (unlimited for general partners vs limited); legal entity (no separate entity vs separate legal personality); membership (limited number vs minimum two, no maximum); capital (partners' contributions vs public share issues); management (partners vs board of directors); continuity (ends on death/withdrawal vs perpetual succession); publication of accounts (private vs published); transfer of interest (consent needed vs shares freely transferable)
6 marks: (b) Any three, 2 marks each: issue of shares to the public; debentures; bank loans and overdrafts; retained profits; trade credit; rights issue; hire purchase/leasing
4 marks: (c) Any two, 2 marks each: by agreement of partners; expiry of fixed term/completion of venture; death, insanity or bankruptcy of a partner; by court order; when the business becomes illegal
questions.explanation: (a) A partnership is formed by agreement or a deed, its general partners have unlimited liability, it has no separate legal personality, and it ends when a partner dies or withdraws; a public limited company is incorporated with the Corporate Affairs Commission, its members have limited liability, it is a separate legal person with perpetual succession, it is run by directors, its shares are freely transferable and it must publish its accounts. (b) A public company raises capital by issuing shares and debentures, from bank loans, retained profits, trade credit and rights issues. (c) A partnership may be dissolved by mutual agreement, at the end of a fixed term, on the death or bankruptcy of a partner, or by a court order.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a chamber of commerce? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of a chamber of commerce. [8 marks]
(c) Explain three ways in which consumer associations protect consumers. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) A voluntary association of business people (traders, manufacturers, bankers etc.) in an area formed to promote and protect their common commercial interests, e.g. Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (3)
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: organising trade fairs and exhibitions; providing business information and statistics; representing members before government; issuing certificates of origin; settling disputes/arbitration; promoting foreign trade contacts; publishing journals
9 marks: (c) Any three, 3 marks each: educating consumers on their rights; reporting fake/substandard goods to agencies such as FCCPC, NAFDAC and SON; pressing for consumer protection laws; seeking redress for exploited consumers; publicising unfair prices and practices; testing products and publishing results
questions.explanation: (a) A chamber of commerce is a voluntary association of businesses in a town or region that promotes their common interests, such as the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry. (b) It organises trade fairs, supplies commercial information, represents members in dealings with government, issues certificates of origin, arbitrates disputes and links members with foreign partners. (c) Consumer associations educate consumers about their rights, expose fake and unsafe goods to regulators such as the FCCPC, NAFDAC and SON, press for protective laws and help consumers obtain redress.

questions.stem:
The following information relates to the business of Mrs Adaeze Obi, a trader in Onitsha, for the year ended 31 December.
Premises: ₦2,500,000
Equipment: ₦800,000
Stock at 31 December: ₦600,000
Debtors: ₦350,000
Cash: ₦150,000
Creditors: ₦420,000
Bank overdraft: ₦180,000
Stock at 1 January: ₦500,000
Purchases: ₦2,800,000
Sales: ₦3,600,000
Expenses: ₦420,000
Calculate:
(a) fixed capital [2 marks]
(b) circulating capital [2 marks]
(c) capital owned [3 marks]
(d) working capital [3 marks]
(e) cost of goods sold [3 marks]
(f) gross profit and net profit [4 marks]
(g) rate of turnover, to two decimal places [3 marks]
questions.explanation: (a) Fixed capital is premises and equipment, ₦3,300,000. (b) Circulating capital is stock, debtors and cash, ₦1,100,000. (c) Capital owned = total assets ₦4,400,000 − liabilities ₦600,000 = ₦3,800,000. (d) Working capital = ₦1,100,000 − ₦600,000 = ₦500,000. (e) Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases − closing stock = ₦2,700,000. (f) Gross profit = ₦3,600,000 − ₦2,700,000 = ₦900,000; net profit = ₦900,000 − ₦420,000 = ₦480,000. (g) Average stock is ₦550,000, so the rate of turnover is 2,700,000/550,000 = 4.91 times.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe a supermarket. [4 marks]
(b) Explain four advantages of supermarkets to consumers. [8 marks]
(c) Explain four reasons why the wholesaler still survives in Nigeria despite moves to eliminate him. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) A large retail outlet selling mainly food and household goods on a self-service basis, with goods displayed on open shelves, prices marked and payment at checkout points (4)
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: wide variety under one roof; self-service gives freedom of choice; prices clearly marked, no haggling; goods often cheaper due to bulk buying; quick shopping; clean and convenient environment; card/transfer payment accepted; parking facilities
8 marks: (c) Any four, 2 marks each: many small retailers cannot buy in bulk from manufacturers; wholesalers grant credit to retailers; manufacturers prefer to sell in bulk and avoid storage; wholesalers break bulk; they bear risks and store goods; they give market information; poor transport makes direct distribution difficult; they finance producers by paying in advance
questions.explanation: (a) A supermarket is a large self-service shop, often part of a chain, selling food and household goods displayed on open shelves with prices marked and payment at checkouts. (b) Consumers enjoy a wide range of goods in one place, freedom to choose without pressure, fixed marked prices, lower prices from bulk buying, speed, cleanliness and electronic payment. (c) Wholesalers survive because small retailers cannot buy in bulk and need credit, manufacturers want to sell in large lots and avoid storage, wholesalers break bulk, bear risk and store goods, and poor transport makes direct distribution difficult.

questions.stem:
(a) The following figures relate to an imaginary country's foreign trade for one year:
Visible exports: ₦25.4 billion
Visible imports: ₦21.9 billion
Invisible exports: ₦3.2 billion
Invisible imports: ₦6.1 billion
Calculate (i) the balance of trade; (ii) the balance on invisibles; (iii) the current account balance of payments. State whether each is favourable or unfavourable. [9 marks]
(b) Explain the functions of the following in Nigeria's foreign trade: (i) Nigeria Customs Service; (ii) Nigerian Ports Authority; (iii) Nigerian Export Promotion Council. [9 marks]
(c) What is entrepot trade? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) 25.4 − 21.9 = ₦3.5 billion (2), favourable (1)
3 marks: (a)(ii) 3.2 − 6.1 = −₦2.9 billion (2), unfavourable (1)
3 marks: (a)(iii) 3.5 − 2.9 = ₦0.6 billion (2), favourable (1)
3 marks: (b)(i) Customs: collects import/export duties and excise; prevents smuggling and prohibited goods; checks documents; compiles trade statistics (any, 3)
3 marks: (b)(ii) NPA: manages and develops seaports; provides berths, cargo handling, pilotage and storage facilities; regulates port operators (any, 3)
3 marks: (b)(iii) NEPC: promotes non-oil exports; provides export market information; trains exporters; administers export incentives; organises trade missions and fairs (any, 3)
2 marks: (c) Importing goods into a country and re-exporting them, with or without repacking, to other countries (2)
questions.explanation: (a) Balance of trade = ₦25.4bn − ₦21.9bn = ₦3.5bn (favourable). Balance on invisibles = ₦3.2bn − ₦6.1bn = −₦2.9bn (unfavourable). Current account = ₦3.5bn − ₦2.9bn = ₦0.6bn (favourable). (b) The Nigeria Customs Service collects duties, fights smuggling and enforces import and export rules; the Nigerian Ports Authority runs and develops the seaports and their facilities; the Nigerian Export Promotion Council promotes non-oil exports through information, training, incentives and trade missions. (c) Entrepot trade is importing goods for re-export.

questions.topic: Purchase and Sale of Goods in Home and Foreign Trade
questions.stem:
Musa Stores, Kano, ordered from Unity Wholesalers Ltd, Kaduna: 40 cartons of noodles at ₦9,500 per carton and 25 bags of sugar at ₦62,000 per bag. Unity Wholesalers allows 15% trade discount and a further 5% cash discount if payment is made within 14 days.
(a) Calculate (i) the gross invoice value; (ii) the trade discount; (iii) the net invoice value; (iv) the amount payable if Musa Stores pays within 14 days. [10 marks]
(b) Distinguish between trade discount and cash discount. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the following terms: (i) credit note; (ii) pro forma invoice; (iii) E. & O.E. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) 40 x 9,500 = 380,000 (1); 25 x 62,000 = 1,550,000 (1); total = ₦1,930,000 (1)
2 marks: (a)(ii) 15% x 1,930,000 = ₦289,500 (2)
2 marks: (a)(iii) 1,930,000 − 289,500 = ₦1,640,500 (2)
3 marks: (a)(iv) Cash discount 5% x 1,640,500 = 82,025 (2); amount payable = ₦1,558,475 (1)
4 marks: (b) Trade discount: allowed by a seller to a buyer in the same trade off the catalogue price, to allow for profit; shown on the invoice and not entered in ledger (2); cash discount: allowed for prompt payment within a stated period to encourage early settlement (2)
6 marks: (c)(i) Credit note: document sent by seller to reduce the buyer's debt for returns, overcharge or allowance (2); (ii) pro forma invoice: preliminary invoice sent before goods are dispatched, for quotation, prepayment or import licence (2); (iii) E. & O.E.: errors and omissions excepted, allowing the seller to correct mistakes later (2)
questions.explanation: (a) Gross value = ₦380,000 + ₦1,550,000 = ₦1,930,000; trade discount at 15% = ₦289,500; net invoice value = ₦1,640,500; cash discount at 5% = ₦82,025, so prompt payment is ₦1,558,475. (b) Trade discount is a reduction off the list price for traders, to give them a profit margin, while cash discount rewards prompt payment. (c) A credit note reduces what the buyer owes; a pro forma invoice is an advance invoice used for quotations, prepayment or import licences; E. & O.E. reserves the seller's right to correct errors and omissions.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three features each of (i) a current account and (ii) a savings account. [12 marks]
(b) State four forms of electronic banking available to customers of Nigerian banks. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a)(i) Current account, any three, 2 marks each: cheque book issued; withdrawals by cheque at any time; usually no interest paid; overdraft facility possible; bank charges apply; suitable for businesses
6 marks: (a)(ii) Savings account, any three, 2 marks each: interest paid on balance; withdrawals usually without cheques (passbook/card); small minimum deposit; encourages saving; limited number of withdrawals; no overdraft
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: ATM; internet banking; mobile banking app; USSD codes; point-of-sale (POS) terminals; electronic funds transfer/instant transfer; debit and credit cards; SMS alerts
questions.explanation: (a) A current account gives a cheque book, allows withdrawals at any time, usually pays no interest, may allow an overdraft and attracts charges, suiting traders. A savings account pays interest, is operated with a card or passbook rather than cheques, needs a small deposit, limits withdrawals and does not allow overdrafts. (b) Nigerian banks offer ATMs, internet banking, mobile apps, USSD banking, POS terminals, instant transfers, cards and SMS alerts.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following principles of insurance: (i) indemnity; (ii) contribution; (iii) proximate cause. [9 marks]
(b) Mr Eze insured his warehouse with Alpha Insurance for ₦4,000,000 and with Beta Insurance for ₦6,000,000. A fire caused damage of ₦2,500,000. Calculate the amount each insurer will pay. [4 marks]
(c) A shop worth ₦12,000,000 is insured for ₦9,000,000 under a policy containing an average clause. A flood causes loss of ₦4,000,000. Calculate the amount the insurer will pay. [3 marks]
(d) State two reasons why insurance is important to a business. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Indemnity: the insured is restored to the same financial position as before the loss, no profit from insurance (3)
3 marks: (a)(ii) Contribution: where property is insured with more than one insurer, each pays a share of the loss in proportion to the sum it insured (3)
3 marks: (a)(iii) Proximate cause: the insurer pays only if the nearest/dominant cause of the loss is an insured risk (3)
4 marks: (b) Total cover 10,000,000 (1); Alpha 4/10 x 2,500,000 = ₦1,000,000 (1.5); Beta 6/10 x 2,500,000 = ₦1,500,000 (1.5)
3 marks: (c) 9,000,000/12,000,000 x 4,000,000 (2) = ₦3,000,000 (1)
4 marks: (d) Any two, 2 marks each: compensation for losses allows business to continue; encourages investment/risk taking; security for bank loans; protects against liability claims; peace of mind to concentrate on business; required by law for some risks
questions.explanation: (a) Indemnity puts the insured back where he was before the loss, without profit. Contribution makes insurers who cover the same risk share the loss in proportion to the cover each gave. Proximate cause means the claim is paid only if the dominant cause of loss is an insured peril. (b) Total cover is ₦10,000,000, so Alpha pays 4/10 of ₦2,500,000 = ₦1,000,000 and Beta pays 6/10 = ₦1,500,000. (c) The shop is under-insured, so the insurer pays 9/12 of ₦4,000,000 = ₦3,000,000. (d) Insurance compensates losses so the firm can continue, encourages risk taking, serves as security for loans and protects against liability claims.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four functions of the Nigerian Exchange (NGX). [8 marks]
(b) Distinguish among the following speculators: bull, bear and stag. [6 marks]
(c) Bola bought 5,000 ordinary shares of a company at ₦12.50 each and later sold them at ₦15.20 each. While she held them, the company paid a dividend of 80 kobo per share. Ignoring charges, calculate (i) her capital gain; (ii) the dividend received. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each: provides a market for buying and selling existing securities; helps companies and government raise long-term capital; gives liquidity to investors; values securities/price discovery; protects investors through listing rules; encourages saving and investment; serves as an economic barometer
6 marks: (b) Bull buys shares expecting prices to rise in order to sell at a profit (2); bear sells shares expecting prices to fall in order to buy back cheaper (2); stag applies for new issues to sell at a premium as soon as trading starts (2)
4 marks: (c)(i) Gain per share 15.20 − 12.50 = ₦2.70 (2); x 5,000 = ₦13,500 (2)
2 marks: (c)(ii) 5,000 x ₦0.80 = ₦4,000 (2)
questions.explanation: (a) The NGX provides a market for existing securities, helps companies and government raise long-term funds, gives investors liquidity, values securities, protects investors through listing and disclosure rules and indicates the state of the economy. (b) A bull buys expecting a price rise; a bear sells expecting a fall; a stag subscribes for new issues hoping to sell quickly at a premium. (c) Bola gains ₦2.70 on each of 5,000 shares, a capital gain of ₦13,500, and receives dividends of ₦4,000.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a commodity exchange? [3 marks]
(b) Name two commodities traded on commodity exchanges in Nigeria. [2 marks]
(c) Explain three requirements for trading on a commodity exchange. [9 marks]
(d) State three benefits of a commodity exchange to the economy. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) An organised market where standardised commodities, mainly agricultural produce and minerals, are bought and sold, often by contracts for present or future delivery (3)
2 marks: (b) Any two, 1 mark each: maize; sorghum; soybeans; sesame; cocoa; cashew; ginger; paddy rice; gold
9 marks: (c) Any three, 3 marks each: grading of commodities; standardisation of quantity and quality; warehousing in certified warehouses with warehouse receipts; clearing and settlement system; registration of brokers/members
6 marks: (d) Any three, 2 marks each: fair price discovery; reduces exploitation of farmers by middlemen; encourages better quality; provides storage and reduces post-harvest losses; access to finance using warehouse receipts; earns foreign exchange; hedging against price risk
questions.explanation: (a) A commodity exchange is an organised market for trading graded commodities such as grains and cocoa, through spot or future contracts. (b) Commodities traded in Nigeria include maize, sorghum, soybeans, sesame, cocoa and cashew. (c) Produce must be graded and standardised, stored in approved warehouses that issue receipts, and traded through registered members with a clearing system to settle deals. (d) Commodity exchanges bring transparent prices, protect farmers from exploitation, improve quality, reduce post-harvest losses, ease access to credit and allow hedging.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three advantages and two disadvantages of rail transport. [10 marks]
(b) Explain four factors a businessman should consider in choosing a means of transport. [8 marks]
(c) What is a bill of lading? [2 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: (a) Advantages, any three, 2 marks each: carries heavy and bulky goods cheaply over long distances; safer than road; reduces road congestion; fixed timetable/reliability; carries large numbers of passengers
4 marks: (a) Disadvantages, any two, 2 marks each: not door-to-door; fixed routes; high cost of construction; not economical for short distances; limited network
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: cost; speed/urgency; nature of goods (perishable, fragile, bulky); safety and security; distance; reliability; availability of the means; value of goods
2 marks: (c) A document issued by a shipping company to the shipper as receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage and document of title (2)
questions.explanation: (a) Rail moves heavy, bulky goods cheaply over long distances, is safer than road, reduces congestion and runs to timetables, but it cannot give door-to-door service, follows fixed routes, is costly to build and is uneconomic for short trips. (b) The choice depends on cost, speed and urgency, the nature of the goods, safety, distance, reliability and availability. (c) A bill of lading is the shipping company's receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage and a document of title.

questions.stem:
(a) What is warehousing? [2 marks]
(b) Explain four functions of warehousing. [8 marks]
(c) Describe three types of warehouse. [6 marks]
(d) State two advantages of a bonded warehouse to an importer. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) The storage of goods in a building from the time they are produced or imported until they are needed (2)
8 marks: (b) Any four, 2 marks each: storage until needed; price stabilisation; protection of goods from damage and theft; blending, packing and grading; breaking bulk; enables continuous production; seasonal goods available all year
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: manufacturers' warehouses; wholesalers' warehouses; retailers' warehouses; public warehouses; bonded warehouses; cold rooms
4 marks: (d) Any two, 2 marks each: pays duty only when goods are withdrawn (in instalments); goods can be re-exported without paying duty; goods can be repacked/sampled under customs supervision; security of goods
questions.explanation: (a) Warehousing is storing goods until they are needed. (b) Warehouses store goods, stabilise prices by releasing stocks during scarcity, protect goods, allow grading, blending and packing, and break bulk. (c) Types include manufacturers', wholesalers' and retailers' warehouses, public warehouses that rent space to anyone, and bonded warehouses for dutiable imports. (d) Bonded warehouses let importers pay duty in instalments as goods are withdrawn and re-export goods without paying duty.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between informative advertising and persuasive advertising. [4 marks]
(b) Explain four media of advertising, stating one advantage of each. [12 marks]
(c) State two functions of the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria (ARCON). [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Informative advertising gives facts about a product, its price, uses and availability (2); persuasive advertising tries to induce people to buy, appealing to emotions/status (2)
12 marks: (b) Any four media, 3 marks each (1 for the medium and its meaning, 2 for an advantage): newspapers/magazines; radio; television; billboards/posters; internet and social media; cinema; direct mail; transit (vehicle) advertising
4 marks: (c) Any two, 2 marks each: regulates and controls advertising practice; vets and approves advertisements before exposure; registers advertising practitioners and agencies; sets standards and code of ethics; sanctions misleading adverts
questions.explanation: (a) Informative advertising tells consumers about a product, while persuasive advertising tries to make them buy it, often by appealing to emotion or status. (b) Newspapers reach literate readers and can be kept for reference; radio reaches rural and illiterate audiences cheaply in local languages; television combines sight and sound for demonstration; billboards give constant exposure to passers-by; the internet and social media can target particular groups and allow interaction. (c) ARCON regulates advertising, vets adverts before exposure, registers practitioners and enforces its code of ethics.

questions.topic: Marketing Concept and the Marketing Mix (4Ps)
questions.stem:
(a) What is the marketing mix? [3 marks]
(b) Explain each element of the marketing mix, using a new brand of bottled water as an example. [12 marks]
(c) Distinguish between pre-sales and after-sales services. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) The combination of controllable variables (product, price, place and promotion) that a firm uses to satisfy target customers and achieve its objectives (3)
12 marks: (b) 3 marks each: product (quality, packaging, brand, bottle sizes); price (pricing to cover cost and match buyers and competitors); place (distribution channels, outlets, availability); promotion (advertising, sales promotion, personal selling, publicity)
5 marks: (c) Pre-sales services are given before purchase to help the buyer decide, e.g. advice, demonstration, samples (2.5); after-sales services are given after purchase, e.g. delivery, installation, warranty repairs (2.5)
questions.explanation: (a) The marketing mix is the blend of product, price, place and promotion a firm uses to satisfy its customers. (b) For bottled water, the product decision covers purity, bottle sizes, labelling and brand; the price must cover costs and compete with rivals; place involves distributors, shops, kiosks and supermarkets that make the water available; promotion uses adverts, discounts and sponsorship to win buyers. (c) Pre-sales services help a customer choose, such as advice and demonstration; after-sales services follow a purchase, such as delivery, installation and warranty repairs.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five elements of a valid contract. [10 marks]
(b) Distinguish between an offer and an invitation to treat, giving an example of each. [4 marks]
(c) Explain three ways by which a contract may be discharged. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
10 marks: (a) Any five, 2 marks each: offer; acceptance; consideration; capacity of parties; intention to create legal relations; legality of object; genuine consent/free will; certainty of terms
4 marks: (b) Offer: a definite promise to be bound on stated terms, which becomes a contract when accepted, e.g. a letter offering to sell a car for ₦4,000,000 (2); invitation to treat: an invitation to others to make offers, e.g. goods displayed with price tags, advertisements, catalogues (2)
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: performance; agreement; frustration; breach; lapse of time; operation of law (death, bankruptcy)
questions.explanation: (a) A valid contract requires an offer, an unconditional acceptance, consideration, parties with legal capacity, intention to create legal relations, a lawful object, genuine consent and certain terms. (b) An offer is a firm proposal that becomes binding when accepted, such as a written offer to sell a car at a stated price; an invitation to treat only invites offers, such as priced goods in a shop window. (c) A contract is discharged by performance, by agreement, by frustration, by breach or by operation of law.

questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between commercialisation and privatisation. [4 marks]
(b) What is deregulation? [2 marks]
(c) Explain four advantages of privatisation to the Nigerian economy. [8 marks]
(d) Explain three disadvantages of deregulation of the downstream petroleum sector to consumers. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: (a) Commercialisation: public enterprise remains government-owned but runs on commercial lines, covering costs and making profit without subsidy (2); privatisation: transfer of ownership (all or part) of public enterprises to private investors (2)
2 marks: (b) Removal of government controls and restrictions on prices, entry and operations in an industry so that market forces operate (2)
8 marks: (c) Any four, 2 marks each: improved efficiency and service; reduction in government subsidies; revenue for government; attracts private and foreign investment; wider share ownership; reduced political interference/corruption; promotes competition and technology
6 marks: (d) Any three, 2 marks each: higher pump prices; higher transport fares and general inflation; price fluctuations with crude oil prices and exchange rates; possible exploitation by marketers; hardship on low-income earners
questions.explanation: (a) Commercialisation keeps a public enterprise in government hands but requires it to operate profitably, while privatisation sells all or part of it to private investors. (b) Deregulation removes government controls on prices and entry so that market forces decide. (c) Privatisation improves efficiency and services, ends drains on the budget, raises revenue, attracts investment and technology, spreads share ownership and reduces political interference. (d) Deregulation of petrol supply exposes consumers to higher and fluctuating pump prices, higher transport fares and inflation, and hardship for low-income earners.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four functions of management. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the following terms: (i) span of control; (ii) delegation of authority; (iii) organisational chart. [6 marks]
(c) Explain three ways in which a company can show social responsibility to its host community. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
8 marks: (a) Any four, 2 marks each: planning; organising; staffing; directing/leading; co-ordinating; controlling; motivating; budgeting
6 marks: (b)(i) Span of control: number of subordinates directly supervised by one manager (2); (ii) delegation: passing authority to a subordinate to perform a task while the superior remains accountable (2); (iii) organisational chart: diagram showing the structure of the firm, its departments and lines of authority (2)
6 marks: (c) Any three, 2 marks each: providing amenities (schools, health centres, water, roads); employing local people; scholarships and skills training; protecting the environment/avoiding pollution; supporting local businesses; producing safe goods at fair prices; paying taxes honestly
questions.explanation: (a) Managers plan by setting objectives, organise resources and structure, staff the firm, direct and motivate workers, co-ordinate departments and control performance against plans. (b) Span of control is the number of people reporting directly to a manager; delegation passes authority for a task to a subordinate while the manager remains accountable; an organisational chart is a diagram of the firm's departments and reporting lines. (c) A company shows social responsibility by providing amenities, employing and training local people, awarding scholarships, avoiding pollution and dealing fairly with customers and government.
